name: CED - South Burlington
old_description: Our local strength scales to the national level – an account at CED Burlington plugs you into our network throughout the country, gaining you access to the hard-to-find items you need to get you off the job site.
about:
CED Burlington operates from Williston, Vermont, as part of a national electrical distribution network that traces its roots to 1957 when the first Consolidated Electrical Distributors (CED) location opened in California. The company has since grown to nearly 800 branches across the United States, each empowered to make local stocking and service decisions while leveraging the broader organization’s purchasing power.

The Williston branch stocks and supplies a wide range of electrical equipment including gear packages, service entrance materials, load centers, disconnects, meter mains, and circuit breakers with GFCI, AFCI, and dual-function variants. Beyond product distribution, the location provides value-added services: a licensed lighting designer develops multi-layer residential lighting plans; estimators perform takeoffs from electrical drawings; project managers offer custom reporting with shipping dates and delivery tracking; and the facility provides customer storage with staged delivery to job sites. Emergency same-day delivery and after-hours weekend availability are also offered.

The branch primarily serves residential and commercial electrical contractors, positioning itself as the “Residential Contractors’ Supplier of Choice.” Its gear package capabilities also support larger commercial and industrial projects requiring service entrance equipment and switchgear. Contractors rely on the branch for both standard stock items and hard-to-find components sourced through the national CED network.

CED’s founding motto—“Service. Integrity. Reliability.”—drives its operational philosophy. Local managers have authority to tailor inventory and services to their market, while the national footprint enables next-day UPS Red Label shipping on many items and access to products from virtually any major electrical manufacturer. The combination of local autonomy, a licensed lighting designer on staff, and a commitment to emergency delivery distinguishes the Williston location in the Vermont market.

old_description: Dump buggy tumblers have been specifically designed to revolutionize mixing processes in food, beverage and pharmaceutical manufacturing, our dump buggy tumbler offers high quality consistent and safe mixing of products such as pasta salads, RTE (ready to eat) meals and protein products like chicken, ribs, and pork loins.
about:
CM Process Solutions LLC is based in Winchester, Kentucky. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The company designs and manufactures dump buggy tumblers for mixing, coating, marinating, and infusing products such as pasta salads, ready-to-eat meals, and proteins including chicken, ribs, and pork loins. Its product line also includes stainless steel hygiene equipment, lifting and dumping systems, and industrial washing machinery. The tumblers use a bi-directional rotation method without paddles or blades and offer vacuum-assist marination. A newly commissioned demonstration center allows customers to test equipment before purchase.

CM Process Solutions serves hygiene-conscious industries across North America, with a focus on food processing, beverage, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. Its customer base includes meat and poultry processors, as reflected by associate memberships in the American Association of Meat Processors and the U.S. Poultry & Egg Association. The company works with industry leaders to develop custom equipment as well as standard solutions.

The company emphasizes innovation in sanitary equipment design, supported by a dedicated team of engineers, sales, and service associates. It differentiates itself through custom-made equipment, a demonstration center for process validation, and partnerships with major food-processing trade organizations.

name: CNC Electronics Inc
old_description: Fanuc parts and repair specialist to the machine tools industries of America and Canada. CNC Electronics Inc are leading independent Fanuc part specialists offering Fanuc parts such as GE Fanuc drives, servo and spindle units, ALPHA and BETA series amplifier module.
about:
CNC Electronics Inc was founded in 2004 in Charlottesville, Virginia, to supply and repair Fanuc components for machine tool users across the Americas. The founders chose the location for its proximity to GE Fanuc Automation, establishing an East Coast hub that now serves thousands of customers in the United States and Canada.

The company specializes in Fanuc drives, servo and spindle amplifiers (including ALPHA and BETA series), control PCBs, power supply units, AC motors, and CNC monitors. It operates an exchange program for emergency breakdowns, a repair service with a typical 24‑ to 48‑hour turnaround, testing, and a surplus channel for obsolete or damaged units. In‑house built CNC monitors for Fanuc, Mazak, and Siemens controls carry a two‑year guarantee, while all Fanuc parts carry a 12‑month warranty.

Customers are primarily machine‑tool builders, job shops, and maintenance departments in the U.S. and Canada that run CNC equipment with Fanuc controls. The firm also directs Western‑region inquiries to a separate affiliate, CNC Electronics West Inc.

The business was started to provide an independent, responsive source for Fanuc parts and repairs, emphasizing quick turnaround, same‑day shipping, and warranty coverage that reduces downtime for manufacturers.

The firm delivers a range of electrical construction and service work, including lightning protection, medium-voltage systems, design-build projects, and general electrical installation. Clients span commercial, industrial, and manufacturing sectors, as well as construction and telecommunications firms. Reference customers cited by the company include R&O Construction, Northern Construction, Boeing, and City Light & Power.

CTI Electric emphasizes honesty, transparency, and a culture of care for employees and partners as its differentiating values. It also highlights its Lightning Protection Institute certification and the use of specialty-certified tradespeople as factors that set it apart.

name: Cablecraft Motion Controls
old_description: In a world on the go, failure is not an option. That’s why, for over seventy years, Cablecraft has specialized in designing engineered solutions that keep things moving, reliably. But we don’t just manufacture quality motion control products and assemblies—our engineering and manufacturing experts collaborate with you to design answers to your most pressing motion control problems.
about:
Cablecraft Motion Controls traces its lineage to 1920, when J.J. Tourek Manufacturing Co. began producing precision screw-machine components in Chicago. The Cablecraft brand itself was founded in 1949 in Tacoma, Washington, as a specialist in aircraft cable assemblies. A third strand, Superior Ball Joint Corp., started in Fort Wayne, Indiana, in 1954. These operations were later combined with Cable Manufacturing & Assembly to form the current entity, now headquartered in St. Matthews, South Carolina.

The company designs and manufactures control cables (push and push-pull), rod ends, ball joints, mechanical linkages, and remote actuation products. It also produces mechatronic assemblies — electronic controls, mechanical systems, and electro-mechanical components — for vehicle platforms. Engineering and manufacturing teams work together to develop proprietary components that reduce design cycles, tooling costs, and total product cost, and they deliver assemblies ready for installation.

Cablecraft serves aerospace (sport aircraft), powersports, construction equipment, light-vehicle, and engine-control markets. Customers range from OEMs seeking standard catalog parts to engineering teams requiring custom motion-control solutions for mission-critical applications.

The firm emphasizes an application-focused philosophy: its engineers partner with customers early to solve motion-control problems rather than simply sell parts. This approach, backed by more than 75 years of combined experience, aims to provide ideas, advice, and engineered solutions that improve precision and reliability.
